title: Base change of a first order thickening, with its ideal sheaf
statement: Let $i:W\to W'$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{W'}\to i_*\mathcal O_W)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfies $\mathcal I^2=0$, i.e. $W\subset W'$ is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let $p:Z'\to W'$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $Z=Z'\times_{W'}W$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $p$ and $i$, with projections $j:Z\to Z'$ and $q:Z\to W$, so that $p\circ j=i\circ q$. Then $j$ is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf is $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}=\operatorname{Im}(p^*\mathcal I\to p^*\mathcal O_{W'}\to\mathcal O_{Z'})$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], [def-pc-module-pullback], and $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'})^2=0$; that is, $Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening and $(q,p):(Z\subset Z')\to(W\subset W')$ is a morphism of thickenings.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening; proof omitted in the source), with Schemes, Lemma 01JU (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-immersion) part (1) for the ideal sheaf Im(g^*I -> O_Y) of a base-changed closed immersion (literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex)

proof.text: (*$j$ is a closed immersion.*) By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applied to the closed immersion $i:W\to W'$ and the morphism $g=p:Z'\to W'$, the projection $W\times_{W'}Z'\to Z'$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The fibre product is symmetric up to the unique isomorphism over both factors given by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], and under it this projection is $j:Z=Z'\times_{W'}W\to Z'$; a closed immersion composed with an isomorphism is a closed immersion. So $j$ is a closed immersion, and $p\circ j=i\circ q$ by the definition of the fibre product. Let $\mathcal I_j=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z'}\to j_*\mathcal O_Z)$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; it remains to show $\mathcal I_j=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$ and $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'})^2=0$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (schemes-lemma-fibre-product-immersion) (1), first sentence; Morphisms, Lemma 01QR (literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex)

proof.text: (*Local picture over an affine open of $W'$.*) Let $V\subseteq W'$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_{W'}(V)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $K=\mathcal I(V)\subseteq A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) the open subscheme $i^{-1}(V)$ of $W$ is affine and $i^\sharp_V:A\to\mathcal O_W(i^{-1}V)$ is surjective, with kernel $\mathcal I(V)=K$ by the definition of the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; hence (the parenthetical of that node) $i^{-1}(V)\to V$ is isomorphic over $V$ to $c_K:\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, Spec of the quotient map. Put $U'=p^{-1}(V)$, an open subscheme of $Z'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] for $j$ and $U'$, the square ($j^{-1}(U')\to U'$, inclusions into $Z$ and $Z'$, $j$) is cartesian; pasting it [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] on top of the cartesian square defining $Z$ ($j$, $q$ over $p$, $i$) shows that $j^{-1}(U')$ with $j|:j^{-1}(U')\to U'$ and $q|$ is a fibre product of $p|_{U'}:U'\to W'$ and $i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] for $i$ and $V$, $i^{-1}(V)$ is a fibre product $W\times_{W'}V$; since $p|_{U'}$ factors through $V$, pasting [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] (the square of $j^{-1}(U')$ over $U'\to V$, $i^{-1}(V)\to V$, placed over the cartesian square of $i^{-1}(V)\subseteq W$ over $V\subseteq W'$, whose outer rectangle is the cartesian square just found) shows that $j^{-1}(U')$ is a fibre product $U'\times_V i^{-1}(V)\cong U'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/K)$, with $j|$ the first projection [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (1) and its proof (the question is local; Lemma 01JR lemma-open-fibre-product for the open pieces); written out by the agent since Stacks argues via Lemma 01HP (lemma-restrict-map-to-closed) in locally ringed spaces

proof.text: (*The ideal of $j$ on affine opens.*) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1) with $S=V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X=U'$, $f=p|_{U'}:U'\to V$ and the ideal $K$: by step 2, $X_K=j^{-1}(U')$ and $j_K=j|_{j^{-1}(U')}$, so for every affine open $U\subseteq U'$, with $B=\mathcal O_{Z'}(U)$ an $A$-algebra via $\rho_{V,U}=(p^\sharp_V)|_U:A\to B$, the ideal sheaf of $j|$ has sections $KB$ on $U$. The ideal sheaf of $j|_{j^{-1}(U')}:j^{-1}(U')\to U'$ is $\mathcal I_j|_{U'}$: for $U\subseteq U'$ both are the kernel of the same map $\mathcal O_{Z'}(U)\to\mathcal O_Z(j^{-1}U)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Hence $\mathcal I_j(U)=\rho_{V,U}(\mathcal I(V))\,B$ for all affine opens $V\subseteq W'$ and $U\subseteq p^{-1}(V)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (1): the ideal of X x_S Y -> Y is Im(g^*I -> O_Y); affine form Spec(B/KB), Algebra tensor with a quotient

proof.text: (*$\mathcal I_j=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$.*) $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_{W'}$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1) for $f=p$ and $\mathcal J=\mathcal I$, the image $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$ of $p^*\mathcal I\to p^*\mathcal O_{W'}\to\mathcal O_{Z'}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], [def-pc-module-pullback] is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'})(U)=\rho_{V,U}(\mathcal I(V))B$ for affine $V\subseteq W'$ and affine $U\subseteq p^{-1}(V)$ (the same map $\rho_{V,U}$ as in step 3). So the subsheaves $\mathcal I_j$ and $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$ of $\mathcal O_{Z'}$ have the same sections on every $U$ in the set $\mathfrak B$ of affine opens of $Z'$ mapped by $p$ into an affine open of $W'$, which is a basis of the topology of $Z'$ (for $z\in Z'$ choose an affine $V\ni p(z)$, then an affine $U\ni z$ inside the open $p^{-1}(V)$). Two subsheaves of a sheaf agreeing on a basis are equal: a section of one over an open $O$ restricts on a cover of $O$ by members of $\mathfrak B$ to sections of the other, and these glue in the other since it is a sheaf and the gluing in $\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is unique. Hence $\mathcal I_j=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01JU (1): 'X x_S Y -> Y corresponds to the sheaf of ideals Im(g^*I -> O_Y)'

proof.text: (*$(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'})^2=0$.*) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (2) with $n=2$, $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'})^2=\mathcal I^2\mathcal O_{Z'}$; the powers there (image of $\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal K'\to\mathcal O$) are those of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], which gives that description as equivalent. Since $\mathcal I^2=0$, $\mathcal I^2\mathcal O_{Z'}$ is the image of $p^*0=0$ ($p^*$ is additive, a left adjoint [def-pc-module-pullback]), i.e. $0$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. (Directly on $U\in\mathfrak B$: $(KB)^2$ is generated by products $(k_1b_1)(k_2b_2)=\rho(k_1k_2)b_1b_2$ with $k_1k_2\in K^2=\mathcal I^2(V)=0$, so $(KB)^2=0$.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening), first order case; proof omitted in the source, written out by the agent

proof.text: (*Conclusion.*) By steps 1, 4 and 5, $j:Z\to Z'$ is a closed immersion whose ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z'}$ has square zero, so $Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (2) (hence a thickening, by the parenthetical of (3) there). As $p\circ j=i\circ q$, $p$ maps $Z$ into $W$ and $p|_Z$ factors as $q$ through the closed subscheme $W$, which is the definition of a morphism of thickenings $(q,p):(Z\subset Z')\to(W\subset W')$ (More on Morphisms, Definition 04EX (5)).
